title: Workforce Intelligence & Analytics Manager
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. </strong></p> <p><strong>We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. </strong><br><strong> </strong><br><strong>We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.</strong><br><strong> </strong><br><strong>Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. </strong><br><strong> </strong><br><strong>For more information, visit <a href="https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwpp.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7CErica.Durr%40wpp.com%7C9bf4566a65bc46a48ac008de749116ea%7C150b5e663d884dee83f6ed149b727a00%7C0%7C0%7C639076363668176216%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Q9juosud56XGLThSFZ1NpPZd6FXpJPxV74OeRZWoh%2B4%3D&reserved=0" target="_blank">WPP.com.</a></strong><br><strong> </strong></p></div><h1>About WPP</h1> <p>WPP is the creative transformation company. Through One WPP and the Elevate28 transformation agenda, we are building a simpler, more integrated, agile and AI-powered enterprise. WPP’s Performance & Culture Center of Excellence brings together the capabilities that help our people, teams and organisation perform, grow and thrive. Within it, Enterprise Effectiveness aligns WPP’s organisation, workforce and teams around its strategic priorities and enables the change required to deliver them.</p> <h1>About the Role</h1> <p>The Workforce Intelligence & Analytics Manager is a contract role that will build the evidence base for the workforce and organisation decisions that matter most to WPP. This role will turn fragmented people, organisation and business data into clear insight, forward-looking scenarios and practical recommendations that help leaders decide where to invest, how to shape the workforce and how to organise for performance.</p> <p>Reporting to the Global Head of Enterprise Effectiveness, you will support the wider Performance & Culture Center of Excellence while working closely with business, People & Culture, Finance, Data and Technology partners. You will establish a trusted workforce-intelligence capability that supports strategic workforce planning and informs priority organisation, workforce, team and people decisions across Enterprise Effectiveness and the wider Performance & Culture Center of Excellence. This is not a traditional reporting role. It combines strategic analytics, internal consulting and leadership of a four-person data and reporting team based in India. You will be expected to work through ambiguity, connect disparate data and systems, and progressively turn fragmented analytics into a more integrated, trusted and usable capability. As a contract appointment, the initial focus will be to establish the core workforce-intelligence approach, strengthen the India-based team and deliver insight against WPP’s highest-priority workforce and organisation questions.</p> <h1>Why This Role Matters</h1> <p>WPP’s transformation requires faster, better choices about work, skills, capacity, organisation and investment. Those choices cannot be made from disconnected dashboards or backward-looking metrics alone. In this role, you will create a more integrated view of the workforce, translate evidence into choices and trade-offs, and help leaders anticipate the implications of AI, changing client demand and new ways of working. The work will directly shape how WPP builds the capabilities, capacity and organisation required for Elevate28.</p> <h1>What You’ll Do</h1> <h2>Build a trusted workforce intelligence capability</h2> <ul> <li>Working with the Global Head of Enterprise Effectiveness, shape and build an enterprise workforce-intelligence approach that connects people, organisation and business data to the decisions leaders need to make.</li> <li>Define a focused set of workforce and organisational measures, dashboards and decision-support tools, moving reporting from activity and headcount toward capacity, capability, cost, productivity, risk and value.</li> <li>Partner with data owners and technology teams to map fragmented data and systems, define analytical requirements, and strengthen data definitions, quality, accessibility and responsible use, while being clear about limitations and the strength of the evidence.</li> <li>Establish repeatable analytical standards, governance and quality controls so insight is trusted, comparable and usable across WPP.</li> <li>Apply AI and automation to improve how workforce data is integrated, analysed and translated into decision support, while maintaining appropriate human judgement, transparency and responsible-use standards.</li> </ul> <h2>Enable strategic workforce planning</h2> <ul> <li>Help business and People & Culture leaders translate strategy, growth priorities and choices about how work is organised into workforce demand, capability and capacity requirements.</li> <li>Build scenarios that show the implications of different choices, including developing, hiring, accessing external capability, automating, augmenting, redeploying and exiting work or roles.</li> <li>Assess the current workforce and future talent supply, including critical skills, capacity, cost, location and role mix, highlighting gaps, risks and investment priorities.</li> <li>Connect workforce planning to business and financial planning cycles so decisions are timely, owned and grounded in common assumptions.</li> </ul> <h2>Deliver forward-looking insight and decision support</h2> <ul> <li>Use statistical analysis, forecasting and scenario modelling to identify emerging workforce and organisational risks, opportunities and patterns.</li> <li>Bring structure to ambiguous business questions, identify what can be answered with available data, test hypotheses and distinguish meaningful signals from correlation or noise.</li> <li>Turn analysis into clear choices, trade-offs and recommendations for senior leaders, including the consequences of action and inaction.</li> <li>Develop concise executive narratives and visualisations that make complex findings understandable without oversimplifying them.</li> </ul> <h2>Strengthen organisation and transformation decisions</h2> <ul> <li>Provide analytical support for organisation design, organisational health, inclusion and impact, talent development, team effectiveness and change priorities across Performance and Culture.</li> <li>Create baselines and evaluate whether organisation and workforce interventions are improving the intended outcomes.</li> <li>Combine quantitative evidence with qualitative insight to explain not only what is happening, but why it matters and where targeted action is needed.</li> <li>Identify enterprise patterns across businesses, markets and functions and convert them into practical recommendations for leaders and Enterprise Effectiveness partners.</li> </ul> <h2>Scale tools, capability and adoption</h2> <ul> <li>Build practical tools, templates and self-service products that improve the quality and consistency of workforce decisions.</li> <li>Coach People & Culture and business partners to interpret workforce insight, challenge assumptions and use scenarios in decision-making.</li> <li>Create a clear intake and prioritisation approach that focuses analytical capacity on the highest-value enterprise questions.</li> <li>Continuously improve the offer through user feedback, adoption evidence and emerging practice in workforce analytics, AI and organisational science.</li> <li>Lead and develop a four-person data and reporting team based in India, setting clear priorities, strengthening analytical and consulting capability, and shifting delivery from fragmented reporting toward higher-value workforce intelligence and decision support.</li> </ul> <h1>Minimum Qualifications</h1> <ul> <li>Relevant experience applying data and analytics in finance, commercial, operational or other business settings, together with experience in people analytics, workforce intelligence or strategic workforce planning.</li> <li>Experience translating business questions into analytical approaches, workforce scenarios and decision-ready recommendations.</li> <li>Strong capability in data analysis, forecasting, modelling and visualisation, using appropriate business intelligence or analytical tools.</li> <li>Proven experience working through ambiguity and improving a fragmented data and analytics environment by connecting disparate sources and systems, strengthening definitions and quality, and establishing practical governance, privacy and ethical standards.</li> <li>Ability to communicate complex findings clearly and influence senior stakeholders in a complex organisation.</li> <li>AI fluency, including a practical understanding of how AI and automation can improve analytics, workforce planning and decision support, and how they may reshape work, skills, roles and workforce requirements.</li> <li>Experience leading and developing an analytics or reporting team, including setting priorities, assuring quality and building capability across locations.</li> <li>A degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent practical experience.</li> </ul> <h1>Preferred Experience</h1> <ul> <li>Experience applying financial, commercial or operational analysis to workforce investment, capacity, productivity or organisation decisions.</li> <li>Experience in a complex global, matrixed or multi-business organisation, ideally supporting enterprise transformation or significant workforce change.</li> <li>Proficiency with relevant business intelligence, data-visualisation or analytical tools, which may include Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Python or R.</li> <li>Postgraduate study or relevant professional qualifications in analytics, finance, strategic workforce planning or a related field.</li> </ul> <h1>What Success Looks Like</h1> <ul> <li>A clear enterprise workforce-intelligence proposition focused on the workforce and organisation decisions most critical to One WPP and Elevate28.</li> <li>A more integrated and trusted data foundation, with common definitions, practical governance and decision-support tools that connect workforce, organisation, business and financial insight.</li> <li>Workforce plans, scenarios and recommendations that materially improve decisions about skills, capacity, location, cost, AI and automation, technology and workforce shape.</li&

title: Software Engineer Summer Intern, AI Compute Libraries & Performance 2027
description: <p><strong>Location:</strong> Bristol, UK<br><strong>Salary: </strong>£2500 per month<br><strong>Start date: </strong>June 2027<br><strong>Application deadline</strong>: Midnight, 29th November 2026 <br><em>We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline.</em></p> <h3>The Internship Programme at Graphcore</h3> <p>Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.</p> <h3>What you’ll work on</h3> <p>Use your programming skills and curiosity to help AI models run efficiently on next-generation Graphcore hardware. </p> <p>In AI Compute Libraries & Performance, you’ll contribute to C++ libraries and compute kernels for machine learning workloads. Your work will include: </p> <ul> <li><strong>Developing compute kernels:</strong> Implement and improve operations such as matrix multiplication (GEMM), convolutions, reductions, elementwise operations and fused kernels that combine multiple operations. </li> <li><strong>Understanding and improving performance:</strong> Use profiling and microbenchmarks to measure execution speed and investigate how threading, cache locality, memory layout and kernel launch efficiency affect performance. </li> <li><strong>Checking correctness and reliability:</strong> Build regression tests and numerical checks, investigate issues and improve the quality of the libraries our customers use. </li> </ul> <p>Through these projects, you’ll develop practical experience connecting numerical computing with how code runs on hardware, helping deliver software that is fast, accurate and reliable. </p> <h3>Your team and support</h3> <p>You’ll join a team building high-performance compute libraries that help customers get more from Graphcore hardware. Our work brings together machine learning, numerical computing and accelerator performance, with colleagues sharing their expertise to solve engineering problems.</p> <p><span data-contrast="none">You’ll contribute to clearly scoped projects and build your skills with guidance from engineers working in performance and low-level software. Together, we use profiling, experiments and technical reviews to compare approaches, understand trade-offs and improve our solutions.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">Your buddy will help you settle in, get familiar with our tools and ways of working, and find the right people to ask. Your manager will meet with you regularly to agree goals, offer feedback and discuss your development, including time for learning.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">We welcome different perspectives and make space for everyone to contribute. Questions, alternative approaches and requests for help are part of how we work. As you take on more responsibility, your colleagues will help you work through challenges, and your ideas will be listened to and discussed respectfully.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <h3>How you’ll learn and grow</h3> <p>Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build performance engineering skills through hands-on work on compute kernels, benchmarks and tests.<span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Profiling and experiments will help you understand where time is spent and how changes to code and data layout affect performance. Numerical validation and regression testing will show you how to check that an optimisation preserves correct results and continues to work as software changes.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Working with specialists and discussing technical trade-offs will help you develop your engineering judgement, explain your findings and connect mathematical operations to efficient implementations on hardware.</span></p> <h3>What we're looking for</h3> <ul> <li>Currently studying towards a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Maths, Machine Learning, Data Science or a related field</li> <li>Experience with C or C++11, plus familiarity with Python or scripting tools for automation and testing</li> <li>An understanding of linear algebra, numerical methods or scientific computing</li> <li>Problem-solving skills and collaborative approach to unfamiliar technical challenges</li> </ul> <p>Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned.</p> <p>Coursework or experience with machine learning frameworks, parallel programming, code optimisation, maths libraries or performance analysis would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements.</p> <h3>Benefits</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Flexible working:</strong> Find a balance between your internship and life outside work</li> <li><strong>5 days of annual leave:</strong> Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship</li> <li><strong>Life in the office:</strong> Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista</li> <li><strong>Learning and development:</strong> Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform</li> </ul> <p>We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.</p> <p>We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.</p> <h3>Sponsorship</h3> <p>Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.</p> <h3>Introduction to Graphcore</h3> <p>At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier.<br>Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.</p> <h3>How to apply and what to expect </h3> <p>To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.</p> <p>Curious about where your skills could take you? <strong>Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.</strong></p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Mobile Developer - L5
description: 📍 Manchester (Hybrid, up to 4 days WFH) | 💰 £75,000 Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology. Our products, Street.co.uk and Spectre form a powerful duo, working harmoniously together to transform an agent's job. From securing more leads and winning new instructions to streamlining business operations and growing market share, our products are supercharging 1,000s of agencies across the UK. How we work in 2026 Engineering at Street Group has changed. Most of us don't write code by hand day-to-day anymore - agents do; we direct. For our mobile team, that shifts where the value is: when AI handles more of the code, what matters most is how the app looks, how it feels, what it does for the user and the ideas you bring to it. Understanding the product and the people using it sits at the heart of the role: we expect engineers to know why they're building something, not just how. Being genuinely tuned into AI tooling is core to the role here, not a side skill and if you'd rather not work this way, that's fair but we're probably not the place for you. Equally, if you see mobile engineering as getting code onto a screen and calling it "good enough", this probably isn't the role for you either. We're a small, autonomous mobile team working on what we think is the best PropTech app on the market. There's no micromanagement and no fixed sprint rituals: when a new project kicks off we get together as a "three amigos" with product and design, get the first tickets out, then keep the conversation going as the work develops. You'll have dedicated backend, design and product colleagues alongside you, and full freedom over how you work. If you love autonomy, are naturally curious, and want to have a genuine impact within a growing company, we think you'd fit right in! Here's what you can expect to be working on as a Mobile Developer (L5) at Street Group Owning the end-to-end delivery of significant features in our React Native app: scoping the problem, directing the build, testing, shipping and iterating based on what you learn. Directing agent sessions to deliver work, while your own attention goes on the user experience, platform feel and the decisions where your judgement is required. Making every experience feel natural on both iOS and Android - understanding what users on each platform expect, and building for it. Looking after the live app: monitoring, stability and our weekly releases across the App Store and Google Play. Defining what success looks like before you build, analysing how features perform after release, and proactively bringing the results - good or bad, backed by data - to product and design. Being a regular voice in product discussions: taking a loose "what if we..." idea and turning it into a strong first version. Picking up tech debt and spotting improvements alongside your main feature, keeping the app maintainable and extendable. Helping to shape new mobile work as it expands across more of the business, including consumer monetisation and lettings. A bit about you You have commercial experience building and shipping production apps with React Native and TypeScript, on both iOS and Android. You work AI-natively as a default, using tools like Claude Code fluently - and you understand what the AI produces well enough to explain and own it. If your current employer doesn't allow AI tools, we'd expect you've been exploring them in your own time. You have strong product and design sense: you're user-focused and care about how something feels to use, not just whether it works. You take quality seriously - your work is tested, solid and thought through before it ships. You've looked after a live app and see its stability, monitoring and releases as part of your job. You're comfortable working independently with loose guidelines, and you're a confident communicator who'll share ideas and challenge in discussions. Experience using analytics to measure features and inform what comes next is a bonus. Why join Street Group? 🏠 Hybrid-working - you can work from home up to 4 days per week 🏖️ Guilt-Free R&R - £1000 towards a holiday after your first year with the team (we'll even cover the tax!) 💪 Joining a culture that supports your development and encourages growth 📚 £500 yearly L&D budget for your career development 🎂 Your birthday on us - we pay, you stay away 🙋 'Give something back' - 2 paid days volunteering on us 👶 Enhanced maternity, paternity & adoption pay 🧠 Mental health & well-being support via Health Assured 🧘 Regular well-being initiatives 🕒 Flexible working hours 🚂 Public transport season ticket loans 🌷 Paid menopause leave 🌞 Holiday buying scheme 🚀 Joining a new team in an exciting business with huge ambition 👥 Be a part of something bigger - everyone in our team is passionate about improving the entire property industry! It's a huge goal, but it motivates us to do better every single day 👩🏿‍💻 A chance to work on cutting-edge technology 🐶 Comfortable, relaxed office space - office dogs welcome! 🍻 Fully stocked fridge and beers (or an alternative) on us every Friday afternoon 🎊 Company and team off-sites, events and happy hours 🚴 Cycle to work scheme 🚗 Electric car salary sacrifice scheme 🌍 Feel good about sustainability - we're a climate-positive company! Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and were about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria; please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application! Salary £75,000 dependent on experience. However, sometimes the perfect person is far more or less experienced than we anticipated. In these situations, planned ranges go out the window. If you think that might be the case, please apply and just let us know. We care deeply about helping the tech industry become a more inclusive and diverse place and we work hard to lead by example. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a complementary team of employees and building an inclusive environment for all. Candidates must be eligible to live and work in the UK and be able to perform the work specified. Interview Process 4 stages (incl. tech task) = An introductory call with one of our Talent team > Take-home tech task > Technical Interview > Final culture fit interview. We want to make our interviews as inclusive as possible, so if you need any adjustments made, or if there's anything you think we should be aware of during the interview process, please do let us know. A note on using AI in your job application As a fast-moving and rapidly evolving tech company, we embrace the advantages of AI and encourage its use throughout our application process. However, our goal is to get to know and hire the authentic you - your skills, experience, and values. We don't want to hire an AI-generated version of you. We consider AI to be a valuable tool, not something that should overshadow you as an individual. How we use AI in the hiring process Candidate experience is really important to us, and our Talent team use AI notetakers during interviews so they can focus purely on their conversation with you. All hiring decisions are made by humans - not AI. Let us know if you have any questions! Compensation: £60K – £75K Mobile Developer - L5 • £60,000 - £75,000 £60K – £75K Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Revenue Operations Analyst (London)
description: Company Overview Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram. Company Operating Rhythm At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance. Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5. Note: this role is based remotely out of London, UK. Regional Expectations Based in London with strong overlap to customer business hours. Excellent written and spoken English. Additional European languages are a plus. The Opportunity Deepgram is hiring a Revenue Operations Analyst to help build and operate the systems, data, and workflows that power our GTM organization. This is a hands-on role for someone who likes getting into the details: fixing broken workflows, improving data quality, supporting quote-to-cash and usage-based billing processes, and finding ways to automate repetitive work. You’ll work closely with GTM Engineering, Finance, Sales, Customer Success, and Renewals to make our commercial systems more reliable, scalable, and efficient. What You’ll Do Support and improve quote-to-cash workflows, including CPQ, order forms, contract changes, subscriptions, entitlements, and downstream system updates. Partner with Finance and GTM Engineering on usage, billing, and monetization workflows, including reconciliation across CRM, product, billing, and finance systems. Serve as a hands-on Salesforce and GTM systems operator, building reports, dashboards, flows, automations, and system enhancements. Maintain strong data quality and governance across accounts, opportunities, contracts, usage, renewals, and customer records. Troubleshoot and resolve GTM systems and process issues, identifying root causes rather than relying on manual workarounds. Identify repetitive or high-friction workflows and help build automation and AI-enabled solutions to reduce manual effort. Support the systems and reporting used to operationalize forecasting, routing, territory, quota, and commission decisions. Partner with the Director, GTM Engineering on system requirements, testing, implementation, documentation, and ongoing optimization. Help create scalable operating processes as Deepgram grows, while staying close to the day-to-day work that surfaces where systems need to improve. It’s Important to Us That You Have 3–4+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, GTM Systems, Sales Operations, Business Systems, or a related role. Strong hands-on Salesforce experience, including reporting, flows, automation, and data management. Experience working across CRM, CPQ, billing, contract, or other GTM systems. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail. A track record of improving workflows, not just executing existing processes. Comfort using AI and automation tools to reduce manual work and improve operations. Ability to work cross-functionally across GTM, Finance, and technical teams. It Would Be Great If You Had Experience in a usage-based or consumption-based business. Experience with CPQ and contract-generation tools. Familiarity with billing or metering systems. SQL or experience working with GTM/customer data. Experience with tools such as Claude, Cursor, n8n, Workato, Retool, or similar automation environments. Experience in a high-growth SaaS or AI company. Notice : We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @ deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to ----- £67K – £83K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus • Estimated Base Salary £67K – £83K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Data Scientist - Product
description: About Us Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar. Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes. 2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR , with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler. We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law. Joining Legora means three things. We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions. We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback. We grow together: as a team and with our customers. Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts. If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place. The role As a Senior Data Scientist for Product at Legora you will turn data into decisions. You'll sit close to the business, taking questions end-to-end: shaping the metric, modelling the data in dbt, running the analysis, and making the recommendation. You'll pull in new data sources when you need to. Insights are useful; impact is what we hire for. We're an AI-first data team . We believe the data function should be redesigned around what AI now makes possible, not retrofitted with it, and we want someone excited to help define what that looks like in practice. There's no single profile we hire for. Some of us are strongest at data modelling and analytics engineering, some at experimentation and causal inference, some at machine learning, some at stakeholder influence. You'll likely be excellent at one or two of these and competent across the rest. That's the bar. We're a small, centralised team supporting the whole company, hiring for the person , not the seat. title: Member of Scientific Staff, Cell Culture and Functional Assays
description: LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time The opportunity We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders. This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard. About us AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one. We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team. The role You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates. Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift. Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on. Your first 90 days FIRST 30 DAYS ◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run. ◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it. DAYS 30 TO 60 ◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria. ◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you. DAYS 60 TO 90 ◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround. ◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation. Who you are You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run. The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week. We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you. MUST HAVE ◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard. ◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number. ◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation. ◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you. ◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience. NICE TO HAVE ◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade. ◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays. ◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it. ◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation. ◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification. Why this is unusual Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product. That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it. Some people find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are. How we work This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building. We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late. UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows. The team you will join You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on. We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work. Our process Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand. If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide. We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. title: Senior Product Manager, KYB - MoonPay Enterprise
description: MoonPay Enterprise is for builders with something to prove. This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. MoonPay Enterprise is the fund layer built for businesses. We power how stablecoins move through real financial operations: enterprises, fintechs, PSPs, wallets, and marketplaces running their treasuries, their cross-border flows, and their stablecoin operations on us. The goal is to make moving real money at scale as predictable as any other piece of financial infrastructure, with the compliance and controls CFOs need to say yes. AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters. You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together. The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building the rails that businesses run real money on, for humans and agents. MoonPay ranked #2 in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100 , made Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 (Top 25 in Finance), and landed on The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running. About MoonPay Enterprise MoonPay Enterprise is one of the more operationally complex products in the stablecoin space: multiple banking providers, multiple payment rails, a growing partner base across two product lines (Orchestration and Issuance), and an active compliance surface across each. MoonPay Enterprise runs B2B, B2B2B, and B2B2C models. Partners integrate our API. Their customers become direct customers of MoonPay Enterprise for compliance purposes. KYB is the front door. Every partner is a business. Every business customer of every partner clears KYB before a single transaction moves. Today the flow is part automated registry verification, part manual review, with different rules for the US and the rest of the world, and turnaround measured in days. That does not scale to where MoonPay Enterprise is going. KYB has to become a product: measurable, fast, API-first, defensible in front of regulators and banking partners. This is a principal seat. You set the multi-year direction for how businesses enter MoonPay Enterprise, and you own the outcome. What You'll Own KYB product strategy & roadmap Business onboarding end-to-end, across every model MoonPay Enterprise runs: partners onboarding onto MoonPay Enterprise, businesses onboarding directly, and business customers onboarding through partners. Platform altitude. KYB decisions ripple into KYC, Travel Rule capture, banking-provider onboarding, and Issuance partner diligence. Connect the surfaces; don't optimise one in isolation. MoonPay Enterprise runs three KYC delivery models (reliance, outsourcing, hosted). KYB coverage is uneven across them. You decide where it expands and in what order. Genuine product depth on MoonPay Enterprise is non-negotiable. Within weeks you talk fluently about KYB outcomes, UBO requirements, virtual account structures, and API behaviour. From being hands-on, not from documentation. Onboarding funnel & conversion The KYB funnel is yours: pass rate, time-to-verified against a 48-72h target, manual review rate, drop-off per step. Instrument what isn't instrumented. Make approval speed and rejection quality measurable. Then move both. Fix rejection UX. Today a declined business often gets a status without a reason, and the partner escalates to support to find out what is missing. Rejection reasons, retry semantics, and resubmission flows become API surface partners build on. KYB API & partner experience The KYB API surface: statuses, webhooks, document submission, and the edge cases that make business onboarding hard (sole proprietors, corporate shareholders, one person who is UBO, Director, and Representative at once). Partners integrate KYB in weeks and self-serve their onboarding questions. Every "what is missing for this customer" escalation is a product gap. Close it. Compliance as product Turn compliance-approved onboarding matrices into product logic. US and non-US differ: control prong versus directors, when ownership documents are required, self-certification options. Partners should never need to read a matrix. EDD triggers, high-risk classification, prohibited industries, Travel Rule capture: you decide how they show up in the product. Compliance is your sparring partner, not a ticket queue. You shape how policy becomes product. They own the policy. Vendor & provider orchestration The verification stack (SumSub today) and the build-versus-buy calls around it. Cost per verification, automation rate, vendor performance. Know when a second provider, a waterfall, or in-house tooling earns its place. Push automation. Decide where AI-assisted review with a human in the loop replaces manual queues, and prove it does not raise risk. Every new banking provider brings its own onboarding requirements. Keep KYB compatible with every rail without collecting everything from everyone. Who You Are A principal-level PM with real KYB or KYC depth. You have owned onboarding, identity, verification, or risk as a platform, not a feature. High agency. You do not wait for a mandate, a brief, or perfect data. You find the problem, claim it, and fix it. Full autonomy, zero to one. Hand you an unowned surface and you take it from first principles to shipped. No handover document, no waiting for direction. AI-fluent by default. AI tools are your daily instruments for analysis, prototyping, and drafting. You run your own queries; analysis is not something you request from another team. Compliance is a design constraint, not a blocker. You read a requirements matrix and see API design, funnel steps, and copy. You know your funnel cold: pass rate, time-to-verified, manual review rate, cost per verification. At home in API-first B2B. Your users are partner engineers and the businesses behind them, not consumers. You have run verification vendors (SumSub, Persona, or equivalents) and know when to switch, stack, or build. A multiplier for the product team around you. You raise the bar for how compliance-heavy product work gets scoped, specced, and shipped. Bias to action. Reactive stewardship of an existing flow is not what we are hiring for. Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. Please know that this list is indicative, and that we would still love to hear from you even if you feel that you are only a 75% match. Skills can be learned, diversity cannot. title: Senior Project Manager (EMEA or USA)
description: Company Overview: At Panopto, we are the most customer-centric learning technology company in the world. As the leader in visual and audio-based learning , we empower organizations to share knowledge effortlessly in a capture and post-capture world. We don’t just build software; we obsess over our users’ goals to deliver solutions that truly matter. Our mission is simple: to attract the brightest talent, people like you, to Elevate the Craft and do the most impactful work of your career. Panopto is looking for a Senior Project Manager to own the execution behind our product initiatives — from the moment we commit to something through the day customers can use it. Position Summary In this role, you will have the opportunity to do the most impactful work of your career, elevating your craft while contributing to a team that values lifelong learning. As the Senior Project Manager, you'll report to the Program Manager and sit inside the Product team on the R&D side, which means the job runs in both directions. Upstream, you're working with Product Managers, Engineering, and Design to keep committed work moving, dependencies visible, and slippage caught early. Downstream, you're making sure Marketing has positioning, Support knows what's changing, Sales can sell it, and customers hear about it the day it goes live. Most project management roles are one or the other. This one is deliberately both, because the handoffs between them are where things fall apart. You'll take initiatives that start as a paragraph and a target quarter, break them into a plan people can act on, and keep a distributed group of teams moving in the same direction until it's out the door. This role is for someone energized rather than frustrated by ambiguity — you'll frequently be the person who turns "we're doing this next quarter" into a sequenced plan with owners and dates, and then holds everyone to it. You’ll also have opportunities to contribute to other initiatives that directly advance our core values and support you in elevating your craft. How You’ll Contribute In this role, you will have the opportunity to Own the end-to-end plan for assigned initiatives — scope, sequence, dependencies, milestones, and readiness criteria from commitment through release. Break large, ambiguous initiatives into discrete workstreams with clear owners, and keep the group aligned as things shift. Work alongside Product Managers and Engineering Leads to track delivery against commitments, surface slippage early, and keep cross-team dependencies visible and resolved. Facilitate the sessions that move work forward — dependency reviews, cross-team planning, release readiness — and make sure they end in decisions. Translate engineering blockers and technical trade-offs into clear, honest updates for Product leadership and commercial stakeholders. Drive go-to-market readiness with Product Marketing, Sales Enablement, Support, and Customer Success so enablement lands with the release, not after it. Coordinate internal and customer-facing release communications, including release notes. Build the templates, checklists, and repeatable processes that make the next release easier than the last one — using AI tooling to cut the manual overhead. What Success Looks Like Within 3 months: You've built working relationships across Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Support, and you own end-to-end coordination for two or more active initiatives — running the delivery cadence with the dev teams and producing status reporting people actually read. Within 6 months: You're anticipating blockers rather than reporting them, and releases you coordinate go out with GTM readiness in place on day one. Within 1 year: You run our most complex, multi-team initiatives with minimal oversight, and the delivery and launch process you've built is what the rest of the team uses by default. Your legacy: Panopto ships predictably, and every team knows what's coming and what they need to do about it — because you built the system that makes that true. Values in Action Customer First, Always : You proactively surface friction points in the customer experience before they are escalated — and propose solutions, not just reports. Thrive Together : You share work-in-progress for early feedback, knowing that challenge improves the outcome. You separate critiques of ideas from critiques of people. Elevate the Craft : You hold the bar high on your own work and invest in developing those around you. You treat every project as an opportunity to learn something new. Act with Ownership : You define success by outcomes, not activity. You flag problems early and bring a proposed path forward, not just the problem. Clarity Over Complexity : You default to the simpler solution. Your written communication — internal or external — is direct, specific, and free of filler. How We Thrive You'll join a team where we challenge ideas, not people. The Product organization exists to ideate, define, and deliver best-in-class products to our customers — assessing market trends, running competitive and customer research, and ruthlessly prioritizing the opportunities with the highest return. We hold ourselves accountable to outcomes, not activity. The Foundation for Success 6+ years of project or program management experience, with at least 4+ years specifically embedded within a B2B SaaS Product or R&D organization. Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience. Demonstrated experience running delivery with software engineering teams and coordinating the go-to-market side of a product launch. This role does both. Proven experience driving delivery for complex SaaS architectures (e.g., API integrations, multi-tenant cloud platforms, feature flags, continuous deployment release models) . Working understanding of the SaaS product lifecycle and agile delivery practices, with the judgment to adapt the process to the situation rather than apply it by the book. Enough technical fluency to hold a credible conversation with engineers about dependencies, trade-offs, and blockers — you don't need to write code, but you can't be a passenger in the discussion. Proficiency with Jira and Confluence for planning, tracking, and documentation. Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to push back constructively on scope creep. Experience working with distributed teams across multiple time zones. Demonstrated track record of designing, implementing, or improving cross-functional delivery and GTM release frameworks, rather than just executing within existing ones. What Sets You Apart Experience coordinating GTM launch activities with Product Marketing, Sales Enablement, or Customer Success. Experience presenting, reporting delivery health, and managing trade-offs directly with VP and C-level stakeholders. Experience sitting inside a Product or R&D organization rather than a central PMO. Active PMP, PMI-ACP, or CSM certification. Hands-on experience leveraging modern PM stacks (Jira, Confluence) and AI productivity tools to streamline status reporting, documentation, and risk analysis. Prior experience in a Product Operations (ProdOps) function. Familiarity with API-based products, feature flagging, or cloud service constraints. Experience in EdTech or with higher education or enterprise customers. Practical use of AI tooling to accelerate planning, synthesis, and reporting work. Join Us Join Panopto and play a key role in shaping the security foundation of a platform used by millions. If you love threat modeling, automating defenses, guiding engineering teams, and turning compliance standards into practical, scalable security practices, you’ll feel right at home here. The Total Rewards package includes competitive base pay and an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs such as health insurance, flexible spending accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work. This collaborative spirit empowers us to challenge ideas (not people) recognizing that our shared success relies on collective wisdom. So we built a video knowledge management platform that helps businesses and universities improve the way that they train, teach, and share knowledge. description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>About AlphaSense: </strong></h2> <p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 12pt;">AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. partnering with Product and Operations teams to pilot new AI-enabled tools that elevate both efficiency and insight quality.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do:</strong><span class="Apple-converted-space"> </span></p> <ul> <li>Partner with<span class="Apple-converted-space">  </span>the Director of Research to develop and maintain a strategic sector roadmap, which you will identify coverage gaps, and recalibrate project pipelines accordingly.</li> <li>Collaborate closely with the Director of Research to identify and shape content to support revenue-generating efforts such as white papers, webinars, internal and external presentations.</li> <li>Establish and maintain feedback loops with call takers and project teams to enhance the quality and insight of future content.</li> <li>Collaborate with North America directed content teams to ensure high quality output and consistency.</li> <li>Partner with Operations and Product teams to pilot and optimize sectors, proactively surfacing new themes and companies to guide future research focus.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Who You Are:</strong></p> <ul> <li>You have 5–7 years of experience in equity research, leading, mentoring, and developing teams of project managers or analysts.</li> <li>You are skilled at translating strategic objectives into actionable research projects that yield high-impact insights.</li> <li>You possess exceptional organizational, analytical, and critical-thinking skills, able to balance multiple priorities with agility while maintaining high quality standards.</li> Our work spans financial services, with a primary focus on asset management, wealth management, insurance and fintech.<br>Engagements we typically lead include:<br>•    Developing corporate, business-unit and growth strategies for established financial institutions and scaling businesses<br>•    Assessing new markets, customer segments, products and distribution opportunities, and shaping market entry and expansion plans<br>•    Reviewing propositions, commercial models and competitive positioning<br>•    Evaluating inorganic and partnership routes to growth, including where they are a better answer than building organically<br>•    Addressing strategic operating model and organisational questions<br>•    Supporting sponsor-backed businesses with value creation strategy, including growth, pricing, commercial effectiveness, cost reduction, operating model and other post-close strategic priorities<br>•    Translating strategy into clear priorities, investment cases and plans that management teams can act on</p> <p><strong>Key responsibilities</strong><br>Both Engagement Leads and Engagement Directors are expected to lead complex strategy engagements independently. In this role, you will own the full sales cycle—from cold outreach to close—focused  on acquiring new logos and working with existing health customers to help solve more of their problems using elastic. If you excel at navigating new organizations and demonstrating the value of advanced search technology to stakeholders, this is your opportunity to drive our next phase of growth.</p> <p title: Finance Manager
description: What we’re all about Quantexa is a global leader in AI-powered Decision Intelligence. As one of the UK’s fastest-growing technology companies, we’re on a mission to help organisations make better, more trusted decisions. As we continue to grow globally, we’re looking for an ambitious and detail-oriented Finance Manager to join our Financial Reporting team , playing an important role in supporting accurate financial reporting across our growing international business. At Q, we’re looking for people who share that vision — people who are curious, collaborative and excited to make an impact. People like you. The Opportunity. In this role, you’ll take ownership of key areas of the reporting cycle, working across multiple entities to ensure accurate and timely financial information. You’ll bring strong technical accounting expertise, support robust financial controls and help identify opportunities to improve how we operate. You’ll also work closely with colleagues across Finance and the wider business, providing insight and guidance on financial matters and helping to ensure we have the right processes in place to support effective decision-making. What You’ll Be Doing. Support the Month-End: Play a key role in the month-end close alongside the Group Reporting team, owning accruals, prepayments and balance sheet reconciliations for your areas, ensuring accuracy and timeliness. Lead Accounts Payable: Own the end-to-end accounts payable process, from supplier onboarding and invoice processing to payment runs, ensuring suppliers are paid accurately and on time with robust controls in place. Own Project Accounting: Track the financial performance of specific initiatives, ensuring costs are captured, allocated and reported correctly, and providing clear insight to project stakeholders. Manage Travel & Expenses: Oversee travel spend and the travel and expense systems used across the business, maintaining clear policies, driving compliance and identifying opportunities to control costs. Strengthen Our Treasury Function: Contribute to the treasury function by building and maintaining cash flow models, producing cash reporting and forecasts, and managing our day-to-day banking relationships. What You’ll Bring. A professional accounting qualification (CIMA, ACCA or equivalent) Proven experience in an operational finance role, with hands-on ownership of accounts payable, cash management and month-end processes. Hands-on experience building cash flow models and forecasts, and working directly with banking partners. Advanced Excel capabilities and experience tracking and reporting spend at a project or initiative level. Experience managing and developing people and resources within an operational finance team, with excellent communication skills and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment. Bonus Points If You Have: Industry experience within a high-growth tech or SaaS company. Experience implementing or managing travel and expense systems (e.g. Ramp, Navan or similar). Hands-on experience with ERP systems like NetSuite. A track record of automating and improving AP, treasury or expense processes. Our perks and quirks. What makes you Q will help you to realise your full potential, flourish and enjoy what you do, while being recognised and rewarded with our broad range of benefits. We offer: Competitive salary & Company bonus 25 days annual leave (with the option of buying up to 5 days, and rolling over up to 10), plus national holidays + your birthday off! Pension scheme with a company contribution of 6% (when you contribute 3%) Private Healthcare, including dental & optic cover Life Insurance and Income Protection Regularly bench-marked salary rates Enhanced Maternity, Paternity, Adoption, or Shared Parental Leave Well-being days Volunteer Day off Work from Home Equipment Commuter, Tech and cycle to work schemes Free Subscription to a meditation, relaxation and sleep app Continuous Training and Development Spend up to 2 months working outside of your country of employment over a rolling 12-month period with our ‘Work from Anywhere’ policy Team Social Budget & Company-wide Socials Our mission. We have one mission. To help businesses grow. To make data easier. And to make the world a better place. We’re not a start-up. Not anymore. But we’ve not been around that long either. What we are is a collection of bright, passionate minds harnessing complexities and helping our clients and their communities. One culture, made of many. Heading in one direction – the future. It’s all about you. We want you to feel welcome, valued, and respected - because it’s your individuality and passion that make you Q . We see that, and we celebrate it. That’s why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment, continuously improving to ensure everyone belongs. Our recruitment process is designed to be inclusive and accessible. If you need any reasonable adjustments or accommodations, please let our Talent Acquisition Team know - we’re happy to assist. No matter your race, beliefs, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, neurodiversity, or abilities—whoever you are—if you're a passionate, curious, and caring human eager to push the boundaries of what’s possible, we want to hear from you. title: Product Manager

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels. Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet. We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel. As Europe’s number one rail travel app, we serve millions of active customers every week across the UK, France, Italy and Spain, and our platform is central to a seamless, end-to-end travel experience. We’re looking for a Product Manager to help drive revenue growth across one of our key revenue lines, including Partnerships and Insurance, and to help scale these areas significantly over the next three years. You’ll play a foundational role in shaping our monetisation product strategy for the number one travel app in Europe, a business serving tens of millions of users across the UK, France, Spain and Italy. The role combines customer empathy, creative merchandising and commercial thinking to deliver significant, measurable value, and you’ll work closely with teams across the business, including Sales, Partnerships, Finance, Data Science, Design and Engineering, to bring new ideas to market and help them grow. In this role as the Product Manager for Monetisation at Trainline, you will...🚄 Own the monetisation product strategy and roadmap for at least one major revenue stream, such as Partnerships or Insurance, with scope to shape new lines as they emerge. Build a deep understanding of customer journeys and design merchandising experiences, across both app and web, that convert, upsell and delight. Work hands-on to drive revenue: testing, launching and scaling monetisation features that deliver against ambitious growth targets. Continuously evaluate product-market fit, pricing approaches, conversion rates and the underlying economics of each feature to find new ways to create value. Balance quick wins with longer-term capabilities such as segmentation, targeting, pricing flexibility and personalisation. Partner closely with Sales, Partnerships and Finance, as well as Data Science, Design and Engineering, to bring new business lines to market and help them scale. Identify new monetisation opportunities based on customer needs, market trends and competitive insight. Share monetisation best practice across the wider product team, helping to set a high standard for the discipline. We’d love to hear from you if you have...🔍 Experience growing high-performing, revenue-generating product lines, ideally within partnerships, affiliate, insurance or other performance-based models. Strong product instincts and a commercial mindset, with a good sense of what great merchandising looks like and how product can shape customer behaviour. Experience working in high-growth, multi-market consumer tech environments. An interest in experimentation and optimisation, with a focus on achieving measurable results. Experience collaborating with data scientists, designers, engineers and commercial colleagues, balancing different perspectives while keeping sight of the goal. A pragmatic, collaborative approach, comfortable making considered decisions and bringing new ideas to the table. Experience scaling products from early stage to maturity, with an understanding of what it takes to build lasting platform capabilities. It would also be helpful if you have experience with pricing strategy or segmentation models, though this isn’t essential. More information: Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! description: About Lendable Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start: One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK Profitable since 2017 Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot ) So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance . We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days. We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes. Join us if you want to Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1 Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions Build the best technology in-house : we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting About the role Every email and notification we send is part of how customers experience Lendable, and a 5.0★ Trustpilot rating across more than 100,000 reviews sets a high bar for it: communication has to be clear, timely and honest. As our Senior Product Manager for CRM & Growth, you'll own the products and systems that shape how customers hear from us across their lifecycle, from first interaction through to retention and reactivation. Product here isn't backlog grooming. The trade-offs are commercial as much as they are user-facing: engagement, retention, conversion, cost to serve and customer experience all pull against each other, and you'll make the calls. There will always be more good ideas than capacity, so sharp prioritisation is central to the job. The role also has a real technical edge. description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About Telnyx</strong></p> <p><em><span style="font-weight: 400;">Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.</span></em></p></div><p> </p> <h2><strong>The opportunity</strong></h2> <p>We're looking for a Director or VP of Product Marketing to lead that effort globally. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect deep technical understanding with positioning, distribution and commercial results. The title will reflect the experience and scope of the person we hire.</p> <p>A good product story matters, but a story alone isn't enough. The person in this role needs to turn our infrastructure into clear customer problems we solve, compelling reasons to choose Telnyx and practical ways to try it. A great sample application, integration or reference architecture can do more than another 30-slide deck. So can a precise message that reaches a developer at the moment they are deciding how to build.</p> <p>You'll work across Product, Engineering, Developer Relations, Sales and Marketing to bring those pieces together. You'll help shape what we launch, how we explain it, how buyers discover it and how our field teams take it to market.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll build</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A coherent product story. Own positioning, segmentation and competitive differentiation across AI inference, Voice AI, agent and edge infrastructure, communications, networking and wireless. Make the full platform understandable without flattening the technical details that make it valuable.</li> <li>Solutions people can actually use. Drive the packaging of sample apps, reference architectures, integrations, templates and working demos that prove what the infrastructure makes possible. Build repeatable plays for use cases such as contact centers, agent assist and industry-specific workflows. These should accelerate adoption and enterprise sales, not become disconnected software products.</li> <li>Distribution that reaches technical buyers. Shape how we win discovery through product pages, developer content, SEO, answer engine optimization (AEO), technical communities and paid acquisition. You won't necessarily operate every campaign, but you must understand the mechanics deeply enough to direct them: search and answer-engine visibility, technical site structure, intent, targeting, conversion paths, attribution and economics.</li> <li>A field-ready commercial engine. Give enterprise sellers, FDEs and solutions teams the pitches, discovery frameworks, architecture diagrams, competitive proof, demos and ROI narratives they need to generate and advance opportunities. Translate platform capabilities into buying reasons for developers, technical executives and enterprise decision-makers.</li> <li>Launches that translate into adoption. Work with Product and Engineering early, not after something ships. Choose the audience, packaging and launch strategy, then measure activation, qualified demand, field utilization and downstream pipeline. Build an operating cadence that keeps pace with a rapidly changing roadmap.</li> <li>An AI-native PMM team. Use AI research tools, coding assistants, agents and automation as part of everyday work to accelerate market research, competitive analysis, messaging tests, content production, demo development and go-to-market execution. Know when to trust those tools, how to evaluate outputs and where human technical judgment still matters. Lead the team to operate the same way.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>How we'll measure success</strong></h2> <p>The ultimate measure is pipeline. Not the number of launches, assets, impressions or campaigns. We expect this leader to partner closely with Demand Generation and Sales to create measurable, qualified pipeline, improve conversion and accelerate opportunities. Product marketing should be able to show how specific product narratives, solutions, integrations and programs contribute to commercial results.</p> <p>Early wins will look like a dramatically clearer platform story; a small number of flagship use cases with runnable demos and integrations; sellers using consistent, technically credible plays; stronger discovery and conversion from search, AEO and paid channels; and a repeatable link from product launches to adoption and pipeline. We care about what works and scales, not activity for its own sake.</p> <h2><strong>What we're looking for</strong></h2> <ul> <li>You've led product marketing for a complex B2B technical platform, ideally in AI infrastructure, developer tools, APIs, cloud, networking or communications. You can be strategic without becoming removed from the work.</li> <li>You are technically fluent. You can understand architecture, work with APIs or SDKs, interrogate a latency or cost claim and talk comfortably with engineers. You don't have to be a production engineer, but you need to know when a demo is real and when it's just a pitch.</li> <li>You understand modern technical acquisition. You're credible directing AEO, SEO, paid programs and developer-focused content, and can connect channel-level metrics to funnel economics and qualified pipeline.</li> <li>You're already effective with AI tools and agents in your own work. You experiment, build workflows and use the technology to move faster. Familiarity with the limitations and evaluation of AI-generated outputs is as important as enthusiasm for the tools.</li> <li>You write exceptionally well, have strong instincts for enterprise sales, and know how to turn a complex product advantage into a clear reason to buy.</li> <li>You've built or led strong teams, can prioritize across competing launches and products, and enjoy working directly with product leaders and technical builders.</li> </ul> <p>Telecom experience is not required. Technical curiosity, taste, speed and a track record of generating commercial impact matter more.</p> <h2><strong>Why Telnyx</strong></h2> <p>This is a chance to shape the market narrative for a company that owns the underlying network, communications and compute infrastructure it sells. The platform is real, customers are deploying it in production, and the commercial opportunity is substantial. You'll have direct access to senior leadership and the ability to build a PMM function measured by its contribution to growth.</p> <h4><strong>Equal opportunity</strong></h4> <p>Telnyx is an equal opportunity employer.
